system.name: LinkLab 2.0
system.one_liner: a multi-tenant, three-layer (IoT/edge/cloud) programmable IoT testbed for experimenting with edge-cloud integration

components.name: LDC Management Cluster
components.role: management infrastructure in the cloud layer running LDC's controller and monitoring

components.name: Monitoring Server
components.role: collects monitoring data path traffic for system-wide anomaly detection

components.name: LDC Controller
components.role: central controller of the LinkLab 2.0 Device Center, coordinating LDC Servers

components.name: LDC Servers
components.role: Kubernetes-based servers that manage programmable devices across layers

components.name: Programmable Cloud Infrastructure
components.role: cloud compute resources users can program as part of an experiment

components.name: Public Cloud
components.role: third-party cloud services (AWS, Azure, Alibaba Cloud) usable as the cloud node in an experiment

components.name: LinkLab Built-in Cloud
components.role: LinkLab's own built-in cloud infrastructure with general-purpose compute (CPU, GPU)

components.name: LDC Client Cluster
components.role: management infrastructure agents running on the edge layer

components.name: LDC Client
components.role: per-device agent connecting a programmable device to the LDC management plane

components.name: Programmable Edge Devices
components.role: edge hardware users can program as part of an experiment

components.name: Programmable IoT Devices
components.role: IoT hardware users can program or interact with

components.name: Prototyping Devices
components.role: development boards for IoT programming (e.g. CC2650 LaunchPad, TelosB, STM32, AliOS HaaS, ESP32, Arduino, virtual devices)

components.name: COTS Devices
components.role: commercial off-the-shelf smart-home devices (e.g. Philips Hue, Xiaomi Smart Home, Tuya Smart) available for experiments

content.key_idea: LinkLab 2.0 spans IoT, edge, and cloud layers, pairing a dashed-outline management infrastructure (LDC controller/clients) with solid-outline programmable infrastructure at each layer, linked by labeled experimental, control, and monitoring data paths.
content.reading_order: Top-down by layer (Cloud, Edge, IoT); within each layer, management infrastructure (dashed, left) pairs with programmable infrastructure (solid, right), per the top legend.

style.stroke: solid rounded borders for Programmable Infrastructure boxes, dashed rounded borders for Management Infrastructure boxes
style.font: Nimbus Sans, small (~4.5-8pt) labels, bold for layer/box titles
style.arrows: bidirectional double-headed arrows, color-coded and solid vs. dashed per the legend
style.icons: bitmap logos and product photos: cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Alibaba Cloud) and each hardware device (Raspberry Pi, Jetson, Arduino boards, smart-home devices, etc.)

encoding.color_means: blue solid arrows = Experimental Data Path, green dashed arrows = Control Data Path, gold dashed arrows = Monitoring Data Path, per the figure's own legend; solid-outline pill boxes = Programmable Infrastructure, dashed-outline pill boxes = Management Infrastructure
encoding.line_style_means: dashed vs. solid box borders distinguish management from programmable infrastructure; dashed vs. solid arrows distinguish control/monitoring paths from the experimental data path
encoding.emphasis: an explicit shape+color legend at the top lets the reader classify every box and arrow in the three layers below at a glance, without needing to read the body text
reusable_patterns: three horizontally stacked layers (device/edge/cloud) each split into a management column and a programmable-resources column
explicit in-figure legend mapping line color/style and box style to semantic categories
product logos/photos used as icons for real hardware and cloud providers
weaknesses: very icon- and label-dense for a single-column figure
some inter-layer wires (e.g. USB Serial vs. Wireless Channel) are easy to confuse without careful tracing

summary: This figure gives the overall architecture of LinkLab 2.0, a multi-tenant IoT testbed spanning three layers: Cloud, Edge, and IoT. Each layer pairs a dashed-outline Management Infrastructure column with a solid-outline Programmable Infrastructure column, per the figure's own legend. In the cloud, an LDC Management Cluster (Monitoring Server, LDC Controller, LDC Servers) oversees Programmable Cloud Infrastructure spanning public clouds (AWS, Azure, Alibaba Cloud) and LinkLab's own built-in cloud. At the edge, an LDC Client Cluster of per-device agents pairs with Programmable Edge Devices such as a Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA Jetson TX2, and Xavier AGX. At the IoT layer, Programmable IoT Devices include both prototyping boards (e.g. CC2650 LaunchPad, Arduino, ESP32, virtual devices) and COTS smart-home devices (Philips Hue, Xiaomi, Tuya). Color-coded arrows distinguish the Experimental, Control, and Monitoring data paths connecting all three layers over wired, wireless, or USB channels.
